correctness.rationale: The commutator has lower-triangular kernel (d_n-d_j)t^(n-j)/(n+1), giving exact Hilbert–Schmidt energy. For 0<t<1 the shifted-diagonal decomposition converges in every S_s, s>1; the periodic first subdiagonal has divergent harmonic absolute sum, ruling out trace class. At t=1 boundedness follows from Hardy; weakly-null periodic test vectors with sum zero and weighted sum sqrt(NV) prove essential norm>=sqrt(V/2). Finite-section energy splits into u_(n modp)/(n+1)+b_(n modp)/(n+1)^2; zero-mean periodic harmonic sums and trigamma identity give constant L(d). Damped means use f_j(q)=[1-q^j]/[(1-q)j^2], whose sum has log(1/(1-q))+1+o(1) asymptotic. Therefore both advertised expansions and difference A(1-gamma) hold for bounded complex periodic d, including repeated/constant symbols. Independent Fraction checks verified nine exact finite-section identities and p2 alternating residual near 2gamma-pi²/4.
